Compare the CLI lifecycle with a server request lifecycle.
A CLI process receives its prepared inputs; a server integration supplies HTTP context and response handling.
chapters.mistakes: Do not paste PHP into an HTML-only preview expecting a server interpreter. A closing tag can introduce accidental whitespace output. Keep a syntax failure separate from a successful execution that produced the wrong value.

chapters.title: Values, types, strict comparisons and null
chapters.mental:
A value has a type that influences allowed operations and comparison behavior. PHP provides integers, floating-point numbers, strings, booleans, arrays, objects and null among its types. Null commonly represents absence, but its meaning belongs to the application's contract. Zero, an empty string and false are different values and should not be casually treated as interchangeable missing data.

Loose comparison can coerce values before comparison; strict comparison checks both type and value. The string '0' and integer 0 may look similar when printed but are different under strict equality. A form normally supplies strings, so validation and explicit conversion are necessary before treating them as trusted numeric data. Strict typing at function boundaries does not validate arbitrary request arrays.
chapters.anatomy: Use `===` and `!==` when type distinctions are part of the contract. `get_debug_type` helps inspect the type. The null-coalescing operator `??` supplies a default for an absent or null value, while `array_key_exists` can distinguish a present null entry from a missing key. Floating-point values approximate many decimal fractions, so financial examples later use integer minor units.
examples: The printed characters do not determine the comparison semantics.
The application decides whether null is meaningful.
The key exists, but the coalescing expression uses the fallback.
tasks: Predict strict equality for '0', 0 and false.
Each has a different type, so cross-type strict comparisons are false.
Add a typed diagnostic to a value before converting it.
The output identifies the actual type rather than relying on its printed appearance.
Model an optional note without confusing missing, empty and null.
The program documents and checks the chosen interpretation of each state.
Repair a loose comparison that accepts an unintended type.
Use strict comparison after deliberate validation and conversion.
Test zero as a valid numeric boundary.
Zero is retained when the contract permits it, rather than discarded as generic falsy data.
Explain the limited scope of strict_types.
It affects relevant scalar call coercions; it does not replace runtime validation or static analysis.
chapters.mistakes: Do not use empty() as a universal validation rule because it treats several distinct values as empty. Compare floating-point results with an appropriate tolerance when approximation is expected. A type declaration is not an input sanitizer.

chapters.title: Expressions, integer money and deliberate conversion
chapters.mental:
An expression produces a value. Arithmetic operators combine numbers, concatenation joins strings, and logical operators combine conditions. Parentheses make intended grouping clear when an expression mixes operations. Do not assume that familiar-looking operators have the same precedence in every language or version. A readable intermediate variable is often safer than a dense one-line formula.

Many decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly by binary floating point. For a small money example, represent amounts as integer cents and define rounding when converting from external decimal text. This avoids accidentally treating a display string as a precise numeric representation. Integer arithmetic still has limits: values outside the supported range need a different numeric representation or library.
chapters.anatomy: Compute subtotal cents as unit cents times quantity, then add a fixed fee. Validate quantity before multiplication. Use intdiv for deliberate integer division and the remainder operator for the remaining cents. This lesson does not accept arbitrary decimal currency strings; that parser would need explicit scale, sign, range and rounding rules.
examples: The unit is encoded in the variable name.
The total is exactly 375 cents within the integer range.
Integer division and remainder produce two decimal digits.
tasks: Predict 125 cents times three units.
The result is 375 cents.
Add a fixed 50-cent fee with a named intermediate value.
The new total is 425 cents and the unit remains explicit.
Implement a bounded quantity calculation and cents formatter.
Valid quantities produce exact integer totals and two-digit fractional display.
Diagnose a concatenation expression that hides arithmetic grouping.
Use parentheses or intermediate variables to express the intended computation.
Reject a negative quantity and test zero.
Invalid negative input is rejected; zero follows the declared contract.
Explain when integer cents are insufficient.
Different currency scales, huge ranges, exchange rates or fractional-unit pricing require an explicit broader numeric policy.
chapters.mistakes: Do not convert a formatted currency label back into a number by deleting random characters. Avoid claiming floating point is universally bad; it is appropriate for many approximate scientific calculations. Define the precision contract first.

chapters.title: Conditions, loops and bounded control flow
chapters.mental:
Control flow determines which statements execute and how often. A branch chooses among alternatives, while a loop repeats a body for a sequence or condition. A loop needs a termination argument: a bounded collection, an advancing counter or another condition that is guaranteed to change. The classroom enforces execution limits, but a good program should still have its own understandable bound.

Guard clauses reject invalid conditions before the main computation. They reduce nesting and make accepted input clearer. A match expression compares strictly and returns a value; it differs from a switch statement's traditional loose comparison behavior and fall-through possibilities. Use the construct whose semantics fit the task rather than choosing the shortest spelling.
chapters.anatomy: A foreach loop visits array values and can also expose keys. A for loop makes initialization, condition and update explicit. In a match expression, each arm maps a condition to a result, and a default arm handles other values when that is appropriate. Do not silently map invalid input to a valid default if the contract requires rejection.
examples: The loop visits a finite array once.
Strict matching preserves the distinction between labels.
tasks: Trace the accumulator after each iteration.
It progresses through 20, 50 and 65.
Add a guard against negative durations.
Invalid values fail before they enter the total.
Build a bounded weekly-duration summary with a route label.
The total and label follow the declared cases and terminate predictably.
Diagnose a while loop whose condition never changes.
Identify the missing progress step and replace it with a bounded iteration where possible.
Test an empty collection.
The total is zero without a special invalid array access.
Explain match versus switch for a typed mapping.
Match returns a value and compares strictly; switch has different comparison and fall-through rules.
chapters.mistakes: Do not rely on a worker timeout as the algorithm's termination strategy. Avoid changing the collection unexpectedly while iterating. A default arm should not conceal an unknown state that needs an error.

chapters.title: Arrays, records, keys and transformations
chapters.mental:
PHP's array is an ordered map: it associates keys with values and preserves an iteration order. It can represent a list or a keyed record, but these are different data contracts. A list of study rows should not accidentally become an object-shaped JSON value because filtered numeric keys were left nonconsecutive. Key coercion can also matter, so avoid treating arbitrary external strings as interchangeable with integer indices.

Transformations are easier to reason about when they do not mutate the original data unexpectedly. Map computes a derived value for each record; filter keeps records satisfying a predicate. Validate expected fields before arithmetic. A missing key is different from a known null field and should be handled according to the record contract.
chapters.anatomy: Use explicit string keys for records, such as subject and minutes. `array_filter` preserves keys, so `array_values` is useful when the intended result is a fresh list. `array_map` applies a function to values. A foreach by reference can leave a lingering reference to the last item; avoid it unless mutation is necessary and understood.
examples: Keys name the meaning of each value.
Reindexing preserves the intended list shape.
The result uses consecutive list indices.
tasks: Explain how a list differs from a keyed record.
A list models ordered values; a record's named keys identify fields.
Add a second validated study row.
Every row has the declared subject and integer-minutes fields.
Filter and summarize study records without changing the originals.
The derived list contains only qualifying rows and retains consecutive indices.
Diagnose JSON output changing from an array to an object shape.
Inspect numeric key gaps after filtering and reindex when the contract is a list.
Test an empty result and a missing required field.
Empty lists are valid where declared; malformed records are rejected explicitly.
Explain the risk of a lingering foreach reference.
A reference variable can still alias the last element and cause later assignments to mutate it.
chapters.mistakes: Do not assume every array is a list. Avoid weakly typed mixed records whose missing fields become warnings during rendering. Keep mutation deliberate and test the original data after transformations.

chapters.title: Functions, contracts, closures and reusable logic
chapters.mental:
A function gives a named operation explicit inputs and an output. A useful contract states accepted values, returned meaning and failure behavior. Type declarations communicate and enforce part of that contract at runtime, but a positive duration requirement needs an explicit value check in addition to an int type. Small pure functions are easy to test because their result depends on inputs rather than hidden global state.

A closure is a function value that can be passed to another function. Arrow functions capture variables from their surrounding scope by value automatically, while ordinary anonymous functions use an explicit use clause for capture. Avoid hidden mutable dependencies when a simple parameter would make the relationship clearer.
chapters.anatomy: Separate formatting from calculation so each can be tested independently. Return values are not the same as echo output. A function that echoes a result may be difficult to compose, while a function that returns a value lets a caller choose how to display it. Use exceptions for invalid inputs when the contract treats them as errors, and document predictable alternate results when absence is normal.
examples: The range check complements the type declaration.
A valid integer produces a doubled integer; a negative value fails.
The operation is passed as data to a transformation.
tasks: Explain the difference between returning and echoing a value.
Returning supplies data to the caller; echo writes output as a side effect.
Add a value-range guard to a typed function.
The function rejects invalid integers even though they satisfy the declared type.
Build reusable duration calculation and display functions.
Calculations can be tested without capturing output, then formatted at the boundary.
Diagnose a result depending on an undocumented global.
Pass the dependency explicitly or isolate the stateful boundary.
Test zero, a normal value and a negative input.
Each follows the stated contract and the failure is intentional.
Explain when a closure improves a transformation.
A short callback can express a local operation while keeping its inputs and captured context clear.
chapters.mistakes: Do not hide output, database access and validation inside one large function merely to reduce file count. A type declaration cannot enforce every domain rule. Keep function names aligned with the actual responsibility.

chapters.title: Strings, UTF-8, bytes and contextual encoding
chapters.mental:
A PHP string is a sequence of bytes. UTF-8 is an encoding that represents characters using one or more bytes, so strlen counts bytes rather than user-perceived characters. A visible character can also consist of multiple code points, such as a letter with a combining mark. Code-point count and grapheme count are therefore different concepts. Choose the measure that matches the product requirement.

This worker does not assume every optional internationalization extension. The examples use valid UTF-8 and demonstrate byte-level behavior plus a Unicode-aware regular expression. Production text normalization, locale-aware sorting and grapheme handling need deliberate library and extension choices. Do not truncate arbitrary UTF-8 bytes and then assume the result remains valid text.
chapters.anatomy: Use explicit UTF-8 when escaping HTML output. JSON requires valid Unicode data and can fail on invalid UTF-8. A Unicode regular expression with the u modifier interprets the pattern as UTF-8, but it is not a universal grapheme library. Keep validation, normalization and output encoding separate because they solve different problems.
examples: The byte length is 2 for this UTF-8 source character.
The encoder validates its input representation.
The result is valid JSON that preserves the readable Unicode label.
tasks: Predict the UTF-8 byte length of é.
It occupies two bytes in the supplied source encoding.
Encode a Unicode label as JSON with explicit error handling.
The output is valid JSON or a visible encoding exception.
Build a text inspection report that labels bytes honestly.
The program does not present strlen as a count of user-perceived characters.
Diagnose a truncated string that splits a multibyte sequence.
Byte slicing can create invalid UTF-8; use a suitable text-aware operation for the intended unit.
Compare a plain ASCII label and a Unicode label.
The byte counts differ from intuitive character counts when multibyte data appears.
Explain validation, normalization and output escaping separately.
Validation checks a contract, normalization chooses an equivalent representation, and escaping protects a destination context.
chapters.mistakes: Do not promise that a regex character count equals a user's perceived character count. Avoid silently replacing invalid data without a declared policy. Text encoding matters before both rendering and storage.

chapters.title: Structured data, streams and bounded file handling
chapters.mental:
JSON is a data format, not a PHP object model or a validation system. Decoding can produce syntactically valid data with the wrong fields, wrong types or an unexpectedly deep structure. Treat parsing and contract validation as separate steps. The examples use tiny inline JSON and a temporary stream so no host path or persistent file is required.

A stream represents a readable or writable sequence of bytes. File operations can fail, return partial results or expose sensitive data if paths are chosen carelessly. In an application, accept an identifier and map it to an owned location instead of accepting an arbitrary user-supplied filesystem path. Bound size before reading untrusted content into memory, and close resources when finished.
chapters.anatomy: Use JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR so invalid JSON becomes an exception instead of an ambiguous null result. Pass true when an associative-array representation is intended, then validate each required field. `php://temp` provides a temporary stream suitable for this local demonstration. Check resource creation and write results, rewind before reading, and close in a finally block.
examples: Syntactic JSON validity is only the first step.

$data = json_decode('{"minutes":30}', true, 32, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
if (!is_int($data['minutes'] ?? null)) throw new InvalidArgumentException('Expected integer minutes');
The record is accepted only after the field contract passes.
The resource belongs to this process.
tasks: Explain why valid JSON can still be invalid application input.
It may contain the wrong structure, types, ranges or required fields.
Add a bounded decoding depth and explicit parse errors.
Malformed or too-deep input produces an intentional failure.
Parse a small study record and round-trip it through a temporary stream.
The field contract passes and the returned bytes match the encoded value.
Diagnose an empty read caused by the stream cursor position.
Rewind before reading from the beginning.
Reject an unexpected field type and an oversized input string.
The program checks both byte budget and data contract before use.
Explain why user-controlled paths need an ownership policy.
A path can escape the intended data area or expose unrelated files; identifiers should map through a reviewed boundary.
chapters.mistakes: Do not disable warnings to hide failed I/O. A file existing does not prove that its content matches the schema. The lesson's temporary stream does not establish durable persistence across worker runs.

chapters.title: Exceptions, errors and useful failure boundaries
chapters.mental:
An exception interrupts the ordinary flow and can be handled by a matching catch block. It is useful when a function cannot fulfill its contract. A catch block should either recover meaningfully, translate the error into an appropriate boundary response or rethrow it. Catching every failure and returning a normal-looking value can corrupt downstream reasoning.

PHP has different error categories, and not every warning automatically becomes an exception. Runtime configuration and library behavior matter. A production error boundary should avoid exposing stack traces, secrets or internal paths to visitors while retaining an appropriate diagnostic record for maintainers. The local classroom output is a teaching surface, not a production logging policy.
chapters.anatomy: Catch specific exceptions near an operation when a specific recovery exists. Use finally for cleanup that should happen whether the operation succeeds or fails. Keep validation errors distinct from unexpected internal failures. An invalid user field can produce a clear correction; an unavailable database may require a generic retry message and internal diagnosis.
examples: The caller can distinguish invalid input from a normal result.
Zero and negative values raise a declared exception.
Finally expresses ownership of a cleanup step.
The useful error is shown and the final step still runs.
tasks: Trace the statements executed after requirePositive(0).
The function throws, the matching catch runs and finally executes.
Add a specific catch around a recoverable validation error.
The caller presents a correction without hiding unrelated failures.
Build a failure-aware parser with explicit success and error paths.
Valid data returns a result; invalid data produces a clear classified failure.
Diagnose a catch-all that returns zero for every failure.
A fabricated normal value hides the difference between valid zero and broken processing.
Test cleanup after both success and exception.
Owned resources are released in either path.
Explain the difference between learner diagnostics and public production errors.
Detailed local diagnostics support learning, while public responses should avoid sensitive internal detail.
chapters.mistakes: Do not catch Throwable merely to print success. Avoid including secrets in exception messages. A handler that returns a valid-looking fallback must have a genuine domain reason and an observable warning where appropriate.

chapters.title: Objects, constructors and immutable value boundaries
chapters.mental:
A class defines a kind of object, and an object combines state with behavior. Use an object when it makes a domain boundary clearer, not merely because the program has grown. A constructor establishes the initial state. An invariant is a condition that should remain true throughout the object's useful lifetime, such as a nonempty topic and nonnegative duration.

Publicly mutable properties can let callers bypass a carefully checked constructor. A small immutable value object can preserve its contract by validating once and exposing readonly data. Readonly does not make every nested object deeply immutable, and it does not replace validation. Understand the specific language guarantee rather than treating the keyword as a complete architecture.
chapters.anatomy: Constructor property promotion can declare and initialize properties directly in the parameter list. Use explicit types and meaningful names. A method can derive a display label from the stored values without changing them. Prefer composition of small responsibilities over a deep inheritance hierarchy built before requirements are known.
examples: Construction is the point where the invariant is established.
Every successfully created Duration has nonnegative minutes.
The method computes from the object's state.
The value is readable without exposing a mutation operation.
tasks: Name the invariant enforced by the constructor.
A successfully constructed duration cannot begin with negative minutes.
Add a method that formats the duration.
Formatting derives from state without changing it.
Build a validated study-session value object.
Its topic and duration satisfy explicit constructor checks and remain readonly.
Diagnose a setter that allows invalid state after construction.
Every mutation boundary must preserve the invariant, or mutation should be removed.
Test an empty topic and zero duration.
The topic is rejected while zero follows the declared nonnegative policy.
Explain shallow readonly versus deep immutability.
A readonly property cannot be reassigned, but referenced mutable objects can have their own changing state.
chapters.mistakes: Do not build an inheritance tree for every noun. A readonly array cannot be changed through that property, but a readonly property referring to an object does not freeze that object's internals. Keep the claimed guarantee precise.

chapters.title: Interfaces, composition and replaceable dependencies
chapters.mental:
An interface describes operations a caller can rely on without selecting a specific implementation. Composition builds behavior from collaborating objects. Dependency injection means supplying a dependency rather than constructing an unknown global dependency inside the operation. These techniques help when a real boundary varies, such as storage or time, but unnecessary interfaces can add ceremony to a tiny fixed calculation.

A test double supplies a controlled implementation for a test. An in-memory repository can verify application behavior without a database, but it does not prove SQL syntax, transactions or connection recovery. Keep unit evidence separate from integration evidence. The same interface can make both tests possible without pretending they are identical.
chapters.anatomy: Define a repository interface with a narrow operation such as countCompleted. The service receives that interface through its constructor. A memory implementation holds synthetic records for this lesson. The service can then be tested with known data and no network. Later PDO lessons qualify the database boundary separately.
examples: The interface exposes a behavior rather than its storage details.
interface ProgressStore { public function completedCount(): int; }
A caller can request a count without knowing the storage engine.
The service receives its dependency explicitly.
A controlled store makes the summary behavior deterministic.
tasks: Identify the dependency hidden by the interface.
The application depends on progress-reading behavior, not a specific database implementation.
Supply an in-memory store with a known count.
The service output is deterministic and requires no external connection.
Build a summary service with an injected repository.
The same service works with two controlled implementations that satisfy the interface.
Diagnose a test double that returns impossible domain values.
The double should preserve the relevant contract instead of making invalid states look normal.
Test zero completed lessons.
The summary handles an empty state without a special external dependency.
Explain what remains untested by an in-memory repository.
Database queries, schema constraints, transactions and connection behavior require integration tests.
chapters.mistakes: Do not claim database acceptance from a mock. Avoid injecting a giant container that hides dependencies again. Use an interface only when it clarifies a meaningful boundary.

chapters.title: Namespaces, project layout and Composer boundaries
chapters.mental:
A namespace groups names so two libraries can use similar class names without colliding. It is a naming mechanism, not a directory, a security sandbox or an automatic package installer. Autoloading is a separate mechanism that resolves a class name to source when needed. Composer commonly manages package dependencies and generates an autoloader for a project.

A dependency manifest describes requirements, while a lockfile records a resolved dependency set. Reproducible deployment uses the reviewed lockfile and installed artifacts, with an explicit update process for security and compatibility. Opening a lesson must not download packages. The classroom single-file PHP worker has no arbitrary Composer project support, so the runnable example demonstrates namespaces in one file and the project workflow remains an external design.
chapters.anatomy: PHP namespace declarations have placement rules. A bracketed namespace block can coexist with an explicitly bracketed global namespace in a single-file teaching program. Production projects should use a coherent autoloading convention rather than a manual chain of untrusted includes. A user-controlled include path can become code execution, so package and file resolution belong to reviewed application code.
examples: The namespace differentiates this class from another Label class.

namespace Learning;
final class Label { public static function text(): string { return 'Study'; } }
The fully qualified class name is Learning\Label.
This is configuration for a separately prepared project, not a pad command.
The convention maps a namespace prefix to the project's source directory after autoloader generation.
tasks: Explain what a namespace does and does not install.
It groups names; it does not fetch code or create an autoloader by itself.
Compare a short imported name with its fully qualified name.
Both can refer to the same class when the import is explicit.
Design a small project layout with source, tests and a public entrypoint.
Application code and tests stay separate from the server's public document root.
Diagnose a missing class despite a correct namespace declaration.
Check source availability and autoload configuration separately from naming.
Explain why an untrusted include filename is dangerous.
It can cause unintended code to be loaded or executed outside the reviewed project.
Describe a deliberate dependency update and lockfile review.
Resolve changes explicitly, review packages and licenses, test the result and deploy the recorded set.
chapters.mistakes: Do not paste a namespace declaration after arbitrary executable code and expect it to work. The runnable reference illustrates qualified built-in naming and layout data, not an installed Composer project. A lockfile does not eliminate the need for ongoing dependency review.

chapters.title: Dates, time zones and deterministic clocks
chapters.mental:
An instant identifies a point on the timeline. A local date and time require a time zone and can be ambiguous or nonexistent around daylight-saving transitions. A fixed offset such as +00:00 is not the same as a named region with changing rules. Store and communicate the representation deliberately instead of assuming every day has exactly twenty-four local hours.

DateTimeImmutable returns a new object when modified, which reduces accidental changes to a shared value. Deterministic tests use a fixed clock or an injected instant rather than the current wall time. Otherwise a test can change result at midnight or fail only in another developer's time zone. User-facing formatting belongs at the presentation boundary.
chapters.anatomy: Parse a documented ISO-like timestamp with an explicit offset for the basic example. Convert to another zone for display without changing the represented instant. A duration measured in elapsed seconds differs from a calendar operation such as next day in a region. Validate parsing failures and inspect warnings when accepting externally formatted dates.
examples: The offset removes ambiguity from this example.
The timestamp represents noon UTC on the stated date.
The instant stays the same while its local representation changes.
tasks: Explain an instant versus a local clock reading.
An instant is a timeline point; a local reading needs zone context and can be ambiguous.
Convert a fixed instant to a named time zone.
The displayed hour changes but the Unix timestamp remains equal.
Build a deterministic study-session time report.
The output uses explicit time zones and a fixed input suitable for repeatable tests.
Diagnose a test that fails around midnight.
Replace ambient current time with a controlled clock or input.
Compare elapsed seconds with a calendar-day operation near a clock change.
They can represent different elapsed durations; document which the application intends.
Explain why a numeric offset is not a complete regional time-zone rule.
A region can change offsets over time due to daylight saving or policy changes.
chapters.mistakes: Do not hardcode a region's current offset as a permanent rule. Avoid using the current date in a test that claims deterministic output. Parsing a date-looking string successfully does not prove it matched the application's intended format.

chapters.title: Testing PHP: examples, boundaries and contract evidence
chapters.mental:
A test compares an observation with an expected contract. A unit test isolates a small behavior; an integration test exercises a boundary such as a database or HTTP server. Both are useful, and neither should be mislabeled as the other. A reference program that prints a success marker without checking the relevant behavior provides weak evidence.

Good cases include ordinary input, an empty or zero boundary, invalid types or ranges, and a previously observed failure. Tests should explain why the expected result is correct instead of repeating the implementation's internal steps. A function and its test can share the same bug if the expected value is computed using the same faulty algorithm.
chapters.anatomy: This course uses a tiny check function that throws RuntimeException on failure, making behavior independent of whether PHP assertions are enabled. Test exceptions by recording whether the expected exception occurred, then check that flag. Do not catch every exception and treat it as the expected one. Full projects can adopt a prepared testing framework, but no dependency installation is needed here.
examples: The result is hand-derived for a tiny fixture.
The test compares against an independently known answer.
Only the intended exception counts as success.
The invalid-input contract is explicitly exercised.
tasks: Classify a pure-function check and a real database transaction check.
The first is unit evidence; the second is integration evidence.
Add an empty-input test with an explicit expected result.
The test records the domain policy rather than guessing from the implementation.
Create a test table for a bounded study-duration function.
Normal, zero, invalid and boundary cases have independently justified outcomes.
Diagnose a test that catches the wrong exception as success.
Catch the declared exception narrowly and let unexpected failures remain failures.
Temporarily introduce a known bug in a learner copy.
A meaningful test fails for the intended reason, then passes after the repair.
Explain why a passing reference is not a bug-free guarantee.
It qualifies the tested contract and cases; untested integration and environment behavior remain separate.
chapters.mistakes: Do not disable checks to preserve a success marker. Avoid tests tied only to private implementation details. Record skipped surfaces honestly, especially when CLI logic stands in for an HTTP workflow.

chapters.title: Templates and context-specific output escaping
chapters.mental:
A template combines trusted structure with data. If a visitor's text is inserted directly into HTML, the browser may interpret it as elements or script-capable attributes. Output escaping represents the data so it remains data in a particular destination context. It is not a one-time cleanup that makes a value safe everywhere. Keep the original validated value and encode it when crossing the output boundary.

For HTML text and ordinary quoted attribute values, htmlspecialchars with explicit flags and UTF-8 is a useful primitive. It is not a JavaScript-string encoder, a CSS sanitizer or a URL policy. A URL in an href needs a separate scheme and destination decision before attribute escaping. Avoid dynamic inline scripts and styles when a simpler data boundary is available.
chapters.anatomy: Define a small e function that calls htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES, ENT_SUBSTITUTE and UTF-8. Use it only for the contexts described by its contract. The CLI reference prints an HTML string as text so you can inspect the escaped bytes; it does not execute that string in a browser. A server template later uses the same contextual boundary before returning a response.
examples: The angle brackets must remain visitor data.
The output contains <, & and > references rather than live tags.
Only the fixed structure is authored markup.
The greeting structure is fixed and the name stays text.
tasks: Predict the escaped form of a name containing < and &.
The special syntax characters become HTML character references.
Add an escaping helper with an explicit UTF-8 contract.
The helper names its HTML context and handles quotes as well as angle brackets.
Render a study-card template from synthetic untrusted labels.
The structure stays fixed while labels are escaped at output.
Explain why the same helper is insufficient for a JavaScript string.
JavaScript has a different parser and escaping rules; use a dedicated serialization boundary.
Test quotes, ampersands and an attack-shaped tag string.
The resulting HTML string contains escaped data rather than an additional live element.
Explain why validated text still needs output escaping.
A valid name can contain syntax characters that are meaningful in the destination context.
chapters.mistakes: Do not escape data once on input and assume it is safe for SQL, JavaScript and HTML alike. Double escaping can corrupt display while still failing another context. Never label an arbitrary strip-tags operation a complete XSS defense.

chapters.title: HTTP requests, response models and routing
chapters.mental:
HTTP separates a request from its response. A request includes a method, target and headers, and may contain a body. A response includes a status code, headers and body. The method expresses intended semantics: GET should retrieve a representation without requesting a state change, while POST commonly submits data for processing. The server must still enforce its own rules regardless of a client-supplied method or path.

Routing selects application behavior from the request method and path. Keep routing separate from the domain calculation so logic can be tested without a live server. A 404 means the requested resource or route is not found; a 405 means the resource exists but the method is unsupported. The application should not return 200 for every failure merely because it produced a page.
chapters.anatomy: The CLI reference receives a synthetic request array and returns a response array. This is a model of an HTTP boundary, not an actual network exchange. A real adapter would read the server-provided environment, validate it, set status and headers before body output, and send the body. Content-Type should describe the response representation, and error bodies should match the declared format.
examples: The model makes the three response parts visible.
The body is text and the status describes success.
The same path can reject an unsupported operation.
A health retrieval is explicitly distinct from other requests.
tasks: Identify status, headers and body in the response model.
They are separate fields with different protocol responsibilities.
Add a not-found response for an unknown path.
The unknown route returns 404 instead of pretending to be a successful page.
Build a pure router for health and lesson-summary requests.
Known GET routes return their declared representations and unsupported requests are rejected.
Diagnose headers sent after body output in a real adapter.
Response metadata must be established before output begins, subject to the runtime's buffering behavior.
Test a known path with the wrong method.
The route returns 405 and identifies allowed methods where appropriate.
Explain what a CLI response model does not prove.
It does not qualify actual networking, server configuration, cookie handling or browser behavior.
chapters.mistakes: Do not trust a route parameter as an authorized identity. Avoid state changes triggered by GET. A printed response array cannot establish that a real server sent those headers.

chapters.title: Server form validation and redisplay without data loss
chapters.mental:
A server receives untrusted input even when the page supplied a constrained control. A caller can omit fields, send an array where a string was expected, alter a hidden value or bypass the browser entirely. Validate shape, type, length and domain rules before using values. An allowlist defines accepted choices; rejecting only known bad strings is usually harder to reason about.

Separate raw input, validated domain values and rendered output. Keep useful user input for redisplay after a validation error, but escape it in the HTML context. After a successful state-changing POST, a redirect to a GET page can reduce accidental resubmission on refresh. That pattern does not by itself provide idempotency, CSRF protection or authorization.
chapters.anatomy: A pure validator returns a value and an error map. Check is_string before trim or numeric parsing because request fields can be arrays. For an integer text field, define an accepted syntax and range explicitly. The example uses a bounded decimal digit pattern, then converts only after it passes. The CLI inputs model POST data; no form is submitted.
examples: The value must be a string before string operations.
An array-shaped field is rejected without a type error.
Unexpected syntax fails before numeric conversion.
tasks: Predict what happens when a caller sends topic[]=HTML.
The server can receive an array, so a string-shape check is required.
Add an allowlist for supported topics.
Only explicitly declared topic values are accepted.
Build a validator returning cleaned values and field-specific errors.
Valid data has a complete domain value; invalid data has actionable errors and no partial write.
Diagnose trimming an array-shaped request value.
Validate its type before calling a string function.
Test missing fields, arrays, out-of-range minutes and valid data.
Each case returns a deliberate validation result without an uncaught type error.
Explain the limits of POST redirect GET.
It helps refresh behavior but does not replace authorization, CSRF checks or duplicate-operation design.
chapters.mistakes: Do not use hidden inputs as trusted prices or identities. Browser constraints are a convenience, not server enforcement. Avoid silently accepting partially validated records because one field looked correct.

chapters.title: Cookies, sessions and a request-to-request lifecycle
chapters.mental:
A cookie is a small value the browser stores and sends according to its scope and attributes. A common session design stores an unpredictable session identifier in a cookie and keeps application state on the server. The identifier is a bearer credential: possession may allow the server to associate a request with that session. Do not put sensitive application state into an unsigned client value and treat it as trusted.

Session lifetime involves creation, authentication transitions, inactivity, absolute expiry and logout. Regenerating the identifier after privilege changes helps address fixation, but safe concurrency and invalidation policies still matter. HttpOnly limits script access to a cookie, Secure restricts transport to HTTPS, and SameSite controls some cross-site sending behavior. These attributes support different defenses and do not replace authorization.
chapters.anatomy: Configure session behavior before session_start and before output. Prefer cookie-only identifiers and strict session handling. Real session storage can lock during a request, so write-close when the required state update is complete in applications that support concurrent requests. The CLI reference uses a pure state transition to demonstrate expiry; it does not claim to create or test a browser session.
examples: This is server configuration for an external HTTP adapter.
A real HTTPS deployment would apply the cookie policy before starting its session.
Time is supplied so the transition is testable.
The inactivity policy is visible instead of relying on an unspecified browser lifetime.
tasks: Explain which data is in the browser and which is on the server.
The browser normally holds an identifier while server storage holds the associated session state.
Add a fixed-clock inactivity check.
The test can inspect the exact expiry boundary reproducibly.
Model session activity and expiry with explicit state transitions.
An expired session is rejected and a valid activity update preserves the declared identity.
Explain why a client-supplied user id is not a trusted session.
A caller can choose that value unless a server-verified credential establishes the identity.
Test activity exactly at and beyond the timeout boundary.
The implementation follows its documented inclusive or exclusive timeout rule.
Describe a real HTTP session acceptance test.
Observe Set-Cookie, a subsequent Cookie request, identifier rotation, logout and expiry through an owned server.
chapters.mistakes: Do not claim a session works because an array update passed. Secure cookies need HTTPS in the real deployment; a local HTTP teaching fixture must explain its different transport boundary. Never log live session identifiers.

chapters.title: CSRF defenses and deliberate state-changing requests
chapters.mental:
Cross-site request forgery exploits a browser's ability to send credentials with a request that the user did not intend. A state-changing endpoint must distinguish an authorized user's deliberate action from a request induced by another site. A synchronizer-token design stores an unpredictable token in the user's server session and requires the same token in the submitted form or appropriate request header.

The token must be generated with a cryptographically secure source, kept out of URLs and checked before changing state. SameSite cookies and origin checks can add protection but do not eliminate the need to understand the application's request paths. XSS can undermine CSRF defenses because malicious script running in the application's own origin may access tokens or perform actions.
chapters.anatomy: Generate token bytes with random_bytes and encode them for transport. Compare a validated submitted string with the known session token using hash_equals. Reject absent, wrong-type and empty values before a state change. The deterministic CLI fixture uses a clearly fake fixed token to test comparison logic; it is not a production token generator or proof of a browser defense.
examples: The value should be unpredictable and bound to the session.
A real server obtains a 64-character hexadecimal token from 32 random bytes.
The trusted token is the first argument.
Only an exact matching submitted string is accepted.
tasks: Explain why a hidden form field alone does not prevent CSRF.
The server must verify an unpredictable session-bound value, not merely the presence of a field.
Add wrong-type and missing-token rejection.
Array, null and absent values cannot reach a successful comparison.
Build a state-change decision that checks method, token and authorization.
Only a deliberate allowed POST with matching token can reach the mutation branch.
Diagnose a token placed in a URL.
URLs can leak through logs, history and referrers, so use the appropriate body or header channel.
Test mismatched, empty and matching synthetic tokens.
Only the exact nonempty expected token passes the local comparison contract.
Explain the relationship between CSRF, SameSite and XSS.
They are distinct mechanisms; SameSite supports CSRF defenses while same-origin script injection can defeat them.
chapters.mistakes: Do not reuse the fixed teaching token in a live server. Do not let a CSRF pass stand in for authorization. Never mutate state before completing the token decision and then try to undo it afterward.

chapters.title: Password hashing and authentication boundaries
chapters.mental:
Passwords should not be stored as plaintext or encrypted with a reversible key merely so the application can compare them. A password hash is designed to make verification possible without retaining the original password and to impose a computational cost on guessing. Use a maintained password-hashing API rather than inventing a hash-plus-salt scheme. The encoded result records the algorithm and parameters needed for verification.

Authentication establishes an identity claim; it does not decide which objects that identity may access. A complete login flow also needs transport security, rate limiting, useful but nonrevealing errors, session rotation and account-recovery design. One successful hash comparison is only a primitive test, not a complete authentication system.
chapters.anatomy: Use password_hash and password_verify. Allow storage large enough for future encoded formats, and use password_needs_rehash during a deliberate migration policy. Algorithm support and cost depend on the prepared runtime; the example uses bcrypt with an explicit bounded teaching cost. Production parameters require current guidance and measurement. Bcrypt has a byte-length limit that must not be ignored when designing input policy.
examples: The library manages the encoded salt and parameters.
The correct synthetic phrase verifies without storing plaintext.
Verification does not reveal the original phrase.
tasks: Explain hashing versus reversible encryption for passwords.
A password verifier needs a one-way verification representation, not recovery of the original secret.
Verify both a correct and incorrect synthetic phrase.
The library accepts only the correct candidate.
Build a password-verification demonstration without printing the hash or secret.
The output reports the test result while keeping credential-shaped values out of logs.
Diagnose using a general fast hash such as SHA-256 for password storage.
Fast general hashes do not provide a suitable password-guessing cost by themselves.
Explain an algorithm-specific input-length boundary.
The application must account for byte limits such as bcrypt's limit and avoid silent truncation policies.
List the additional controls required around a real login.
TLS, rate limits, session rotation, recovery, safe errors and authorization remain separate requirements.
chapters.mistakes: Never copy the teaching passphrase into a real account or print password hashes as routine diagnostics. Do not invent a manual salt. A stronger hashing parameter cannot compensate for an unbounded public login endpoint.

chapters.title: PDO, prepared statements and the value-query boundary
chapters.mental:
PDO is a database access interface with drivers for particular engines. The classroom prepares PDO SQLite so examples can use an in-memory database without credentials or network access. PostgreSQL and SQLite differ in types, SQL features and concurrency, so a SQLite pass does not prove PostgreSQL behavior. Revisit the SQL route for relational design and engine-specific queries.

A prepared statement separates the fixed query structure from parameter values. A value containing a quote or SQL-looking text remains a value when bound correctly. Parameters cannot stand in for arbitrary identifiers, keywords or sort directions. Dynamic column selection needs an explicit allowlist that maps a choice to trusted SQL structure. Escaping HTML output is a separate boundary after fetching data.
chapters.anatomy: Create a PDO connection with exception error mode, create a tiny schema and prepare an INSERT. Execute it with a parameter map, then prepare a SELECT using a value predicate. Keep the database handle local to this run. The example's table is disposable in-memory state, not the learner's persistent classroom database.
examples: The SQL structure is fixed before the name is supplied.
The apostrophe is stored as data rather than breaking the query.
Parameters do not replace column names.
Only reviewed column names can enter a dynamic query structure.
tasks: Explain what a prepared value parameter can and cannot replace.
It represents data values, not arbitrary table names, column names or SQL keywords.
Insert a title containing an apostrophe.
The stored value round-trips exactly through a bound parameter.
Build a local PDO note store with prepared insert and lookup.
The expected record is retrieved and SQL-looking text remains data.
Diagnose concatenating an untrusted sort key into SQL.
Map the choice through an explicit trusted allowlist rather than treating it as a bindable value.
Test an empty result and an attack-shaped title.
No-match behavior is explicit and the table remains intact after storing the title.
Explain which checks must be repeated when moving to PostgreSQL.
Driver behavior, schema types, SQL syntax, transactions and concurrency need engine-specific integration evidence.
chapters.mistakes: Do not concatenate values into SQL and call the result prepared merely because prepare() is used afterward. Avoid copying SQLite-specific assumptions into PostgreSQL without checking them. Database binding does not make fetched text safe for HTML.

chapters.title: Transactions, constraints and concurrent changes
chapters.mental:
A transaction groups operations into a unit that can commit or roll back. Atomicity means the unit is not partially applied when the transaction aborts under the database's contract. Constraints enforce invariants close to the stored data, where every writer must encounter them. Application checks alone can race when two requests read the same state and then both attempt an update.

Concurrency requires more than wrapping code in begin and commit. Isolation levels, locking and the chosen database determine what other transactions can observe. An optimistic update includes an expected version in its WHERE clause and checks the affected-row count. A zero-row update can mean the record changed or was not accessible; the application must decide how to report and retry safely.
chapters.anatomy: Begin a transaction, perform related writes, commit only after all succeed, and roll back on failure if still in a transaction. Use a database CHECK or UNIQUE constraint where it expresses a durable invariant. The SQLite example demonstrates rollback and a version predicate in one connection; it does not simulate real parallel requests or qualify PostgreSQL isolation.
examples: The version is part of the write condition.

UPDATE
  plans
SET
  minutes = :minutes,
  version = version + 1
WHERE
  id = :id
  AND version = :expected_version;
A stale expected version updates no row.
Failure prevents a partial unit from being accepted.
The transaction is rolled back before the failure propagates.
tasks: Explain atomicity without claiming every transaction is serializable.
Atomicity concerns all-or-nothing application; isolation is a separate property.
Add a database constraint for nonnegative minutes.
The database rejects invalid writes even if an application check is missed.
Implement a version-checked update in a disposable database.
The first expected version succeeds and the repeated stale version affects zero rows.
Diagnose accepting a zero-row update as success.
Inspect affected-row evidence and handle the conflict explicitly.
Force a failure after a write and verify rollback.
The stored value remains the pre-transaction value.
Explain the limits of the single-connection concurrency demonstration.
It tests predicates and rollback, while real races require controlled concurrent integration tests on the target engine.
chapters.mistakes: Do not blindly retry a non-idempotent operation after an ambiguous commit result. A transaction does not eliminate all races under every isolation level. Keep affected-row checks tied to a documented driver and statement contract.

chapters.title: Authorization, ownership and object-level access
chapters.mental:
Authentication answers who the application believes is making a request. Authorization answers whether that identity may perform this action on this object. A record id in a URL is a locator, not proof of permission. A hidden owner field, disabled button or filtered interface cannot enforce access because the client can alter all of them.

Apply authorization on every relevant server operation, including reads, updates, deletion and exports. Scope queries by trusted identity or enforce an explicit policy before returning data. Deny by default when a required identity or permission is missing. Error behavior should avoid disclosing another user's sensitive record while still providing useful recovery for legitimate users.
chapters.anatomy: The reference receives a trusted synthetic actor id as a separate parameter from the requested record id. A query includes both record id and owner id as bound values. The fake actor is a test fixture, not a login implementation. A real adapter must obtain it from a verified session or credential and must not copy it from a form field.
examples: The owner comes from trusted server identity context.

SELECT
  title
FROM
  notes
WHERE
  id = :id
  AND owner_id = :actor_id;
A record belonging to another actor is not returned.
A requested object is untrusted input; actor identity has a different origin.
The API makes the trust distinction visible.
tasks: Explain why knowing a record id is not sufficient permission.
Ids identify objects; a policy must authorize access for the current actor.
Add owner scoping to a prepared read query.
The query can return only the requested actor's matching record.
Build an object-access function with separate trusted actor and requested id inputs.
The owner can read the record and a different actor receives no record.
Diagnose trusting owner_id from a submitted form.
A caller can forge it; derive ownership from the verified server-side identity.
Test own, other and missing records.
Each follows a deliberate policy without leaking another actor's title.
Explain why hiding an edit button is only a user-interface convenience.
The server endpoint must enforce the same permission even when called directly.
chapters.mistakes: Do not confuse an unpredictable id with an authorization check. Avoid logging sensitive returned data during denied requests. Ensure update and delete paths have the same ownership discipline as reads.

chapters.title: JSON APIs, schemas and consistent error responses
chapters.mental:
An API contract describes inputs, outputs, error behavior and relevant operational limits. JSON is only the serialization format. A client needs to know whether minutes is an integer, whether a field can be null, which errors are recoverable and whether an operation changes state. Adding a field can be compatible for some clients while changing its meaning or type can break them.

Error responses should be structured and consistent without exposing internal exceptions. A validation error can identify fields; an unexpected internal error should provide a safe message and a correlation mechanism in a real deployment. Status codes, headers and body must agree. Returning a JSON error object with an unconditional 200 status makes clients and monitoring misinterpret failures.
chapters.anatomy: Keep a response builder separate from the domain function. Encode with JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR and declare application/json in the real HTTP adapter. Decode test output and inspect types rather than comparing arbitrary whitespace. This CLI lesson models the response; the external HTTP fixture later checks actual status and headers. It does not enable cross-origin access automatically.
examples: The type contract is visible in the record.
Minutes is numeric and complete is boolean, not display strings.
A field map supports useful client feedback.
The error shape is predictable and contains no stack trace.
tasks: Distinguish a JSON number from a numeric-looking string.
30 and "30" have different JSON types and can affect client validation.
Add a consistent error code to invalid-input responses.
Clients can inspect a stable code without parsing human prose.
Build a response model that maps success and validation failure consistently.
Status, content type and JSON body agree with the declared contract.
Diagnose an internal exception serialized directly to a public response.
Translate it at the boundary and keep sensitive details in controlled diagnostics.
Round-trip a Unicode label and a boolean through JSON.
The decoded values retain their intended types and text.
Explain a backward-compatible versus breaking API change.
Compatibility depends on the documented client contract, especially type and semantic changes.
chapters.mistakes: Do not append debugging output before or after a JSON body. Avoid exposing raw exception messages. A local encode/decode test does not prove actual Content-Type or status headers on a server.

chapters.title: Pagination, caching and bounded application workloads
chapters.mental:
An endpoint should not assume its dataset will remain small. Bound the amount of work and the response size. Pagination returns a portion of a collection under a documented order. Offset pagination is simple but can shift as records are inserted or removed. Cursor pagination identifies a position in a stable ordering and needs a tie-breaker when the primary sort value is not unique.

Caching reuses a previous result, but the cache key and invalidation policy are part of correctness. A key that omits user identity or authorization scope can expose another user's data. A stale result may be acceptable for one display and harmful for another. Define freshness, ownership and failure behavior before using a cache to hide an expensive query.
chapters.anatomy: The reference demonstrates a bounded in-memory cursor over unique increasing ids. It validates the page size, selects ids greater than the cursor and takes only the requested count. This is an algorithm model, not a database query plan or distributed cache. A production query needs a matching index and engine-specific measurement.
examples: The id is both unique and ordered in this small model.

SELECT
  id,
  title
FROM
  notes
WHERE
  owner_id = :actor
  AND id > :after_id
ORDER BY
  id ASC
LIMIT :page_size;
A scoped ordered page can continue after the last seen id.
The key includes the context that changes the result.
Different actors and data versions do not accidentally share one entry.
tasks: Explain why pagination needs an explicit stable order.
Without it, page boundaries can duplicate or omit records unpredictably.
Add a maximum page-size rule.
A caller cannot request an unbounded result.
Implement a cursor-based slice over synthetic records.
The second page continues after the last id and the final page can be shorter.
Diagnose a cache key shared by all authenticated users.
The key omits an authorization-dependent dimension and risks data leakage.
Test an empty page and an invalid page size.
Empty results are represented normally while invalid budgets are rejected.
Explain what must be measured before claiming a faster database endpoint.
Inspect the actual query plan, index, workload, latency distribution and correctness under the target engine.
chapters.mistakes: Do not claim a cursor guarantees a snapshot while records change unless the storage contract provides that guarantee. A cache hit can still be wrong. Bound work even for authenticated clients.

chapters.title: PHP milestone: a tested study-planner application core
chapters.mental:
The application core coordinates a use case without pretending to be an HTTP server. It receives a trusted actor identity and untrusted proposed values, validates the proposal, writes through a repository and returns a result. Keeping these boundaries visible makes it possible to reason about what is trusted and which failures prevent a write.

This milestone combines the earlier mechanisms in a small study planner. The database is disposable SQLite memory. The input is synthetic. Validation rejects unsupported topics and out-of-range durations. A prepared statement stores an accepted plan under the supplied actor. A query scopes retrieval by that actor. Rendering and HTTP adaptation remain separate so the same core can later be integrated and tested through a real server.
chapters.anatomy: Write the acceptance matrix before implementation: a valid plan is stored once, invalid input stores nothing, one actor cannot read another's plan, and output has a clear type contract. A production service would add session verification, CSRF where relevant, idempotency, concurrent behavior, migrations and operational controls. Do not infer those properties from this small core.
examples: Identity is supplied by a trusted adapter, not copied from input.
The use-case boundary shows which values require validation.
The test expresses a domain requirement.

Invalid minutes -> validation error -> zero inserted rows
Valid plan -> stored under actor -> visible only to that actor
The core's behavior can be checked without a browser template.
tasks: Draw the trust boundary around actor identity and form values.
The adapter verifies identity; the application validates proposed domain values.
Write the acceptance matrix before implementing the service.
Normal, invalid and cross-owner cases have explicit observations.
Build a tested planner core with validation and prepared storage.
Accepted plans persist in the disposable database and rejected inputs create no rows.
Diagnose a service that writes before validating all fields.
Move complete validation before mutation or ensure a correctly owned transaction aborts the entire unit.
Test cross-owner retrieval and an invalid duration.
No other actor's row is exposed and the invalid request changes no stored state.
Explain the remaining work before this core becomes a deployed application.
Real HTTP, session, CSRF, persistence, concurrency, accessibility and operational acceptance remain separate integration tasks.
chapters.mistakes: Do not add a success banner that claims the user now has a production service. Preserve invalid cases in the test suite. A synthetic trusted actor is a testing input, not an authentication implementation.

chapters.title: A real local HTTP lab: sessions, forms and persistent notes
chapters.mental:
The earlier PHP pads isolated language and application logic. A real HTTP lab adds a browser, request headers, cookies, server process and persistent storage. Each boundary introduces behavior that a pure function cannot prove. The maintained optional fixture runs a local PHP development server in its own Linux container and binds its published port to host loopback. It is a learning server, not an internet deployment.

The fixture stores synthetic notes under an anonymous browser session. That demonstrates session continuity and separation, not verified user identity. A session cookie carries an identifier; the server stores the session and a random owner key. Prepared statements store notes in SQLite. A form includes a CSRF token, the server validates it before writing, and successful POST handling redirects to a GET page. Source, database and session state have distinct lifetimes.
chapters.anatomy: Read the fixture README and copy the lab into an ignored learner directory before editing. Its Compose project name is ds60-web-study and its loopback port is 18088. Inspect whether those names belong to existing work before starting. The fixture builds only when you deliberately run the documented command. It does not mount the Docker socket, contact the classroom database or expose a public port. Named volumes retain notes and sessions across container replacement; removing those volumes is a separate reset.
examples: Run from a new learner copy of the fixture after reading its README.

docker compose --project-name ds60-web-study up --build --detach
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:18088/health
An actual bounded HTTP request returns the lab's health response.
The browser network panel exposes the real protocol sequence.

GET / -> HTML form + session cookie
POST /notes with valid token -> 303 Location: /
GET / -> stored synthetic note
The POST and follow-up GET are separate requests.
tasks: Draw the lifecycle from browser cookie to server session to stored note.
The cookie identifies session state; the session supplies an owner key and CSRF token; the database stores the owned note.
Inspect the real Content-Type and redirect status.
Record actual response headers instead of inferring them from PHP source.
Run the owned lab and create one synthetic note through the browser.
The note survives a page reload and appears after a successful POST-redirect-GET sequence.
Submit a request with a missing or wrong CSRF token.
The server returns a rejection and inserts no note.
Stop and resume the lab without deleting volumes.
The same browser session can recover its notes while the named data and session volumes remain.
Explain which properties this local server has not qualified.
It does not establish production TLS, verified accounts, multi-instance concurrency, internet hardening or high availability.
chapters.mistakes: Do not start a second copy on an occupied port or delete an unrelated project to free it. A health response proves the process answered, not that note creation, CSRF rejection and persistence work. Anonymous session ownership must never be described as a production login system.

chapters.title: Uploads, filesystem ownership and outbound side effects
chapters.mental:
Accepting a file creates a new trust boundary. A client-supplied filename, extension and MIME label are untrusted claims. A safe design sets a byte limit, allows only needed formats, checks actual content as appropriate, generates its own storage name and keeps uploads outside executable public directories. An image parser can itself have vulnerabilities, so format validation is part of a broader dependency and isolation policy.

Filesystem paths should be derived from an owned identifier and a controlled root, not concatenated from arbitrary request text. Avoid making user uploads executable or allowing path traversal into application source. Storage quotas, retention and deletion behavior matter because a valid file can still exhaust resources. The default classroom pad does not accept uploaded files, and this lesson does not add an upload endpoint.
chapters.anatomy: PHP's upload APIs distinguish actual HTTP-uploaded files from arbitrary paths, but successful movement does not prove the content is safe. Treat sending email, calling a payment service or publishing a message as explicit side effects with credentials and failure handling. An outbox design can record an intended external action in the same database transaction as a domain update, then process it with idempotency controls. It does not magically make an external network action exactly once.
examples: This is a design fragment, not a complete upload handler.
The original user filename does not choose the server path.
The record expresses an intention awaiting controlled delivery.
A worker can track attempts without pretending the remote effect already happened.
tasks: List the untrusted claims in an uploaded file request.
Filename, extension, declared media type, content and size all require a deliberate policy.
Design a maximum size and allowlist for one required format.
The policy rejects unnecessary formats and enforces a bounded resource budget.
Write an upload design with separate validation, storage and retrieval boundaries.
Files receive generated names, stay outside executable public paths and have ownership and retention rules.
Diagnose concatenating ../../ into a storage path.
User input must not determine an unrestricted filesystem location.
Model a timeout after a remote service may have accepted an action.
The outcome is ambiguous; retries need idempotency or reconciliation instead of assuming failure means nothing happened.
Explain which tests are needed before enabling uploads or email.
Exercise actual HTTP upload handling, malformed content, size limits, ownership, cleanup and controlled external-service failure behavior.
chapters.mistakes: Do not copy this lesson's fragments into a live upload service without the full surrounding contract. Avoid teaching extensions as proof of content type. Never send real email, credentials or files while merely reading a lesson.

chapters.title: Deploying PHP: containers, web servers and operations
chapters.mental:
A production PHP deployment commonly separates an HTTP server or reverse proxy from a PHP process manager. PHP-FPM manages FastCGI workers; it is not itself a general browser-facing HTTP server. A web server routes appropriate requests to the runtime and serves approved static assets. The public document root should contain only files intended for delivery, keeping source configuration, dependency metadata, private data and secrets outside that boundary.

A container packages a runtime and application, while volumes or external storage hold durable state. Rebuilding an image does not migrate a database automatically. A release needs a plan for schema changes, compatibility, rollback, backup and restore. A backup job reporting success is weaker evidence than an actual restore that recreates the expected data and application behavior.
chapters.anatomy: Use reviewed locked dependencies and a deliberate image tag or digest policy. Supply secrets through a controlled runtime mechanism rather than baking them into images or committing them. Enable appropriate error logging without displaying internal stack traces publicly. TLS termination and trusted proxy headers require an explicit network ownership policy; do not trust forwarded identity or scheme headers from arbitrary clients.
examples: This diagram describes responsibilities rather than a ready-to-run production configuration.

Browser -> HTTPS reverse proxy -> PHP-FPM -> application service -> database
                         -> approved static assets
HTTP handling, PHP execution and durable storage are separate responsibilities.

Image built -> container started -> health request answered
Migration checked -> write/read checked -> backup restored -> rollback rehearsed
No single earlier step proves all later application properties.
tasks: Explain why PHP-FPM is not interchangeable with the development HTTP server.
FPM manages FastCGI workers and needs an appropriate HTTP-facing integration.
Draw the public document root and private application directories.
Only intended static assets and entrypoints are directly served.
Design a release plan for the study planner with durable storage.
The plan covers configuration, secrets, migration, health, write/read acceptance, backup and rollback.
Diagnose secrets copied into an image layer.
Removing them in a later layer does not reliably erase earlier layer content; rotate exposed secrets and rebuild correctly.
Describe a restore test in a separate disposable environment.
Recovered data and application behavior must be checked without overwriting the active store.
Explain what evidence is needed before publishing an image as ready.
Source, dependency, runtime, browser, data recovery and target-environment checks need explicit results and limits.
chapters.mistakes: Do not expose the PHP built-in learning server to the public internet and call it a production architecture. Avoid broad prune commands as deployment recovery. A successful image build cannot establish application correctness or backup recoverability.

chapters.title: Integrated capstone: accessible, tested and recoverable web learning
chapters.mental:
The final project joins HTML structure, CSS presentation, browser interaction, PHP application logic and relational storage around one useful learner journey. Start with a small task: create and review a study plan, receive actionable validation feedback and return later without losing the plan. Expand only after the core behavior is explainable and tested. A framework may help organize a larger application, but it does not remove these contracts.

Use a threat model that names assets, actors, trust boundaries and likely failures. For this learning project, synthetic notes are the data asset; anonymous session ownership is an explicit limitation; request fields are untrusted; output, SQL and filesystem access are separate interpretation boundaries. If adding real accounts, the identity and recovery design must be upgraded deliberately rather than quietly inheriting the anonymous demo's assumptions.
chapters.anatomy: Create an acceptance matrix with normal, invalid, cross-session, restart and accessibility cases. Keep unit checks for pure functions, integration checks for HTTP and storage, and actual browser observations for focus and layout. Connect to the JavaScript and D3 path when adding data visualization, to SQL when expanding relational modeling, and to Docker and Kubernetes when studying delivery. Each extension needs evidence for its new boundary.
examples: The case spans multiple layers without confusing them.

Open page -> keyboard-enter plan -> submit -> observe 303 -> read saved plan
Reload -> same session sees plan
New browser session -> original plan is not listed
The observed journey qualifies local session ownership and persistence, not verified account identity.
The report states both completed and unqualified surfaces.

Verified: local request validation, prepared storage, CSRF rejection, keyboard form
Not yet qualified: production TLS, account recovery, multiple replicas, public abuse resistance
The report supports a concrete next step without claiming universal correctness.
tasks: Define one small learner journey and its finish condition.
The journey ends with an observable saved plan and a clear way to recover from invalid input.
Map every input and output to its validation or encoding boundary.
HTML text, SQL values, URLs, session identity and filesystem paths have distinct policies.
Build and review a learner-owned extension of the supplied local lab.
The extension has coherent HTML/CSS, tested PHP behavior and a bounded reproducible setup.
Introduce a controlled invalid request and preserve its evidence.
